newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway Kristin gas, condensate find positive - OD.
newsitem.headline: Norway Kristin gas, condensate find positive - OD.

text.p: The Norwegian Oil Directorate (OD) said on Wednesday that results of production testing at Saga Petroleum's Kristin gas and condensate discovery in the Haltenbanken off mid-Norway were "extremely positive".

The OD said Kristin, in block 6406/2 southwest of the Smoerbukk development, tested from the deepest well at 880,000 cubic metres per day of gas and 840 cubic metres per day of condensate through a 18 millimetre choke.
The shallowest well produced at 750,000 cubic metres per day of gas and 960 cubic metres per day of condensate.
Both reservoir zones contain more condensate than was previously found in the block, the OD said in a statement.
"The drilling indicates at least as big if not bigger resources...than at the considerable Lavrans find, which was discovered in 1995," the statement said.
"The results are considered to be extremely positive and strengthen expectations that the discovery can be exploited," it said.
A spokesman for Saga Petroleum said the company had not released any reserve estimates at the find.

In March Saga said it would evaluate the possibility of laying a pipeline to land condensate from the Haltenbank area in the Norwegian Sea off mid-Norway. If implemented, the pipeline would be the first to shore light oil from this part of the Norwegian continental shelf.
